description: Multi-hop payment paths and their source cost. When to use: Before a cross-currency or multi-hop payment: to see whether a route exists and how much the source would spend to deliver the amount. A call can take up to about 25 seconds and paths may be non-optimal. Prefer another tool: To check whether a direct payment can succeed (use `/v1/xrpl/payment-readiness`), or for the single-hop cost of a trade on one pair (use `/v1/xrpl/slippage`, which compares the order book and the AMM). Example: xrpl_paths {"source":"rvYAfWj5gh67oV6fW32ZzP3Aw4Eubs59B","destination":"rhub8VRN55s94qWKDv6jmDy1pUykJzF3wq","asset":"XRP","amount":"1"}

amount.description: Positive decimal amount of asset the destination receives

asset.description: Asset delivered: `XRP`, or `CODE.issuer`: `CODE` is a 3-character standard code or 40 hexadecimal digits, and `issuer` is a classic XRPL address. Standard codes are case-sensitive: `usd` and `USD` are different tokens, so send the exact code. A standard code uses letters, digits or `?!@#$%^&*<>(){}[]|` and is never `XRP`; percent-encode the symbols in a URL (for example `%3F` for `?`). A 40-hex code is read in any case, and the 40-hex form of a standard code means that code.

destination.description: Receiving account: valid classic XRPL address

send_max.description: Most the source may spend, in send_max_asset; not with source_assets

send_max_asset.description: Asset of send_max; give it with send_max. `XRP`, or `CODE.issuer`: `CODE` is a 3-character standard code or 40 hexadecimal digits, and `issuer` is a classic XRPL address. Standard codes are case-sensitive: `usd` and `USD` are different tokens, so send the exact code. A standard code uses letters, digits or `?!@#$%^&*<>(){}[]|` and is never `XRP`; percent-encode the symbols in a URL (for example `%3F` for `?`). A 40-hex code is read in any case, and the 40-hex form of a standard code means that code.

source.description: Sending account: valid classic XRPL address (r..., checksum verified)

source_assets.description: Comma-separated assets the source may spend (1 to 4); not with send_max. Each asset: `XRP`, or `CODE.issuer`: `CODE` is a 3-character standard code or 40 hexadecimal digits, and `issuer` is a classic XRPL address. Standard codes are case-sensitive: `usd` and `USD` are different tokens, so send the exact code. A standard code uses letters, digits or `?!@#$%^&*<>(){}[]|` and is never `XRP`; percent-encode the symbols in a URL (for example `%3F` for `?`). A 40-hex code is read in any case, and the 40-hex form of a standard code means that code.

name: xrpl_paths

age_seconds.description: Age of our read at response time, not of the ledger close time

as_of.description: When we read the data from the ledger (our read time), not the ledger close time

cache.description: Cache state; a composite answer reports the worst state of its reads, miss above stale

ledger_index.description: Ledger the data comes from; ledger_state says whether it is validated or open; null when no read behind the answer names a ledger, never 0

ledger_state.description: State of the ledger ledger_index names: open for the fee read, which reads the open ledger, else validated; a composite answer is open only when every read is

stale.description: True when served past its fresh TTL (stale-on-error)

alternatives.description: Path alternatives; empty when none was found

cheapest.description: True for the lowest `source_amount` among the alternatives with the same source asset

effective_price.description: The source amount / `amount`: units of `source_amount.asset` per unit of `asset`, an MPT source in its base units (`value_atomic`, no issuance read)

currency.description: Currency code of this step (3 characters or 40 hex)

currency_ascii.description: Readable text of a 40-hex currency code; null when not printable ASCII; absent for XRP and 3-character codes

source_amount.description: Estimated amount the source spends; an MPT in `value_atomic`

currency_ascii.description: Readable text of a 40-hex currency code; null when not printable ASCII; absent for XRP and 3-character codes

value.description: Decimal string in units of `asset`: XRP in XRP, not drops; an issued currency as the ledger holds it; null for an MPT, since this route reads no MPT issuance and so no `AssetScale` (its base units are in `value_atomic`)

value_atomic.description: MPT only: the exact amount in whole base units; absent for XRP and issued currencies

source_any_issuer.description: True when rippled names the source account as the issuer of `source_amount`: the source may spend that currency from any issuer it holds (PathRequest.cpp); false for XRP

suggested_send_max.description: `source_amount` × 1.01, rounded up to the asset precision: whole drops for XRP, whole base units for an MPT (from `value_atomic`) and 15 significant digits for issued currencies

amount.description: Amount queried, in units of `asset`, as the request sent it (echo of `amount`)

asset.description: Asset queried, in the canonical form the route reads: `XRP` or `CODE.issuer` (echo of `asset`)

asset_currency_ascii.description: Readable text of `asset`'s 40-hex currency code; null when not printable ASCII; absent for XRP and 3-character codes

paths_may_be_non_optimal.description: Path finding is best effort: a cheaper path may exist

send_max.description: Amount of `send_max_asset` queried, as the request sent it (echo of `send_max`); null when the request sent none

send_max_asset.description: Asset of `send_max`, canonical (echo of `send_max_asset`); null when the request sent none

send_max_asset_currency_ascii.description: Readable text of `send_max_asset`'s 40-hex currency code; null when not printable ASCII; absent for XRP, 3-character codes and when `send_max_asset` is null

source_assets.description: Assets queried as `source_assets`, canonical, in request order; null when the request sent none
